steps: Coordinator durably records the saga and next command.
Service A commits its idempotent local transaction.
Service B cannot complete, and the failure is recorded.
Coordinator invokes A compensation and records the final saga outcome.

lesson.scenario: Checkout CO-204 coordinates Order, Inventory, and Payment through a durable saga log.
entities: stores commands, replies, and compensation for CO-204

steps.title: Start durable checkout
steps.narration: The saga log records CO-204 and command CreateOrder before sending it.
steps.outcome: The order is visibly PENDING while the checkout continues.
steps.invariant: The saga log persists intent before each externally retried command.

steps.title: Reserve inventory
steps.narration: Inventory commits reservation R-204, reducing available units from 9 to 8.
steps.outcome: A real intermediate hold is visible before payment succeeds.
steps.invariant: Reservation R-204 is idempotent and has a matching release command.

steps.title: Record failed payment
steps.narration: Payment rejects the card and stores DECLINED for stable charge ID PAY-204.
steps.outcome: The failed charge becomes durable before compensation starts.
steps.invariant: A DECLINED charge is never treated as an unknown timeout.

steps.title: Compensate visible effects
steps.narration: The saga releases R-204 and cancels O-204, recording each reverse result.
steps.outcome: Stock returns to 9 and the pending order reaches a truthful terminal state.
steps.invariant: Compensation completes in reverse dependency order and never deletes audit facts.

steps.title: Retry compensation idempotently
steps.narration: After a lost acknowledgement, Release R-204 is retried; inventory returns the prior result without adding stock.
steps.outcome: The retry proves idempotency: available inventory remains 9, not 10.
steps.invariant: Every forward and compensating command is keyed so retries preserve exactly one business effect.
